electric-cooler: Compressor fridge-coolers with built-in or removable batteries for cars, camping and tailgates.

products.name: Anker SOLIX S5000 Portable Power Station, 5,024 Wh LFP, 4,500 W, 120/240 V
specs: 5,024 Wh LFP (314 Ah cells), expandable to 30 kWh with five BP5000 batteries
4,500 W continuous, 8,000 W peak (fraction of a second)
USB-C 100 W, USB-C 15 W, USB-A 12 W
3,000 W total (2,000 W high-voltage + 1,000 W low-voltage)
1,800 W from 120 V; 4,500 W from 240 V (0 to 100% in 99 minutes)
8.8 W (120 V mode), 13.7 W (240 V mode), per Anker
97 lb, 10.6 × 22.0 × 15.2 in, wheels and pull handle
products.summary: The S5000 packs 5,024 Wh and a 4,500 W inverter with a 240 V L14-30 outlet into a 97 lb wheeled box. Its 8.8 W idle draw is the lowest in this class, which matters over a multi-day outage.
products.fit: Households that want the longest runtime per dollar for a well pump, fridge and furnace blower through a 240 V inlet or transfer switch.
caveats: Anker quotes 7 to 8 weeks to ship orders placed on or after 2026-11-01.
Launched 2026-10-27; no independent test reports yet.
The 8,000 W peak lasts a fraction of a second; a pump's start surge has to fit under 4,500 W.
No NEMA 14-50 outlet, and it does not charge below 32 °F.
Only BP5000 batteries expand it; BP3800 and BP3000 packs do not fit.

products.name: Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40L Electric Cooler (42 qt) with 288 Wh Removable Battery
specs: 1 × 288 Wh LFP removable battery included; second bay for a spare
52 h claimed on one battery (Eco mode, 39 °F inside, 77 °F ambient); The Gadgeteer measured about 51 h
AC 95 W, 12 to 30 V car or solar up to 100 W, USB-C 60 W
Just under 50 dB in Max mode (The Gadgeteer)
Anker app over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
products.warranty: Anker 'hassle-free' warranty; length not stated on the product page
products.summary: A compressor cooler with a swappable 288 Wh battery that ran about 51 hours at 39 °F in The Gadgeteer's test. Tom's Guide picked it over the EcoFlow Glacier on battery life and price.
products.fit: Car campers and tailgaters who want fridge-level cold for two days without a power station.
caveats: Cooled to 43.5 °F, not 32 °F, in 15 minutes in The Gadgeteer's test.
Display can read up to 5 °F warmer than the actual interior.
55 lb before food; wheels are a paid add-on.
Single zone; the 58 L model is the dual-zone one.

notes: Brand store ankersolix.com is not Shopify (storecheck 404), so prices were read by WebFetch. Verified 2026-11-06: S5000 $2,499.99 (launch special, $3,599.99 shown struck; ship 7-8 weeks for orders on/after 11-01; 5-year warranty); EverFrost 2 40L $799.99 on the electric-cooler collection page. F3800 Plus and C300 DC pages showed 'Sold Out' and 'Price Loading'; F3000 and C2000 Gen 2 pages showed no price (JS-loaded), so they were not recorded. C1000 Gen 2 already exists as an Amazon record and was not redefined. Rivals verified today: BLUETTI Apex 300 $1,499 (compare $1,699) on bluettipower.com (existing awin slug bluetti-apex-300; its stored price may need refreshing); EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 $2,799 on both us.ecoflow.com and Amazon B0D14FMFZD (74% 5-star, 185 ratings), so Amazon is linked at equal price; DELTA Pro Ultra $3,799 on us.ecoflow.com but marked unavailable, Amazon ASINs blocked, so it is a maker row only. Jackery HomePower 3600 Pro Max: jackery.com returned HTTP 429 on five attempts over 10 minutes and Amazon search returned nothing, so no price is printed and the page tells readers to check Jackery's page; its 14-50R outlet comes from The Solar Lab (50 A 240 V) and a retailer spec sheet, not Jackery's own page, which also rate-limited. Pain points counted across forums, reviews and Q&A: pump start surge tripping the inverter (6 sources), 240 V requirement and 120 V-only confusion (5), transfer switch/inlet needed (4), idle draw (4: Solar Lab Apex 20 W, Solar Lab Jackery 30 W, two Bluetti forum threads), weight/no wheels (4), 120 V/240 V simultaneous limits (3), noise (2), resets/firmware (1), long ship time (S5000 page). Segments: multi-day backup with pump up to 3/4 HP -> S5000 (most Wh per dollar, lowest claimed idle); cheapest/in stock -> Apex 300; proven surge handling -> DELTA Pro 3; 50 A outlet -> Jackery; whole-panel -> DELTA Pro Ultra. Unverified and kept off the page: whether the S5000 runs 120 V and 240 V simultaneously (Anker page shows separate buttons; Gadgeteer says 240 V output stays available while charging from 120 V), exact count of S5000 5-20R outlets (Anker page says two, two reviewers say four), S5000 idle draw (maker claim only), Apex 300 outlet NEMA types (Bluetti page says 30 A/50 A ports only). Amazon record (DELTA Pro 3) contains no dollar amounts. Rakuten gave no codes; the brand site shows only an 'extra 5% off first purchase' sign-up offer with no code, so codes is empty. Reddit was not reachable; owner complaints came from the Bluetti forum, DIY Solar Forum snippets, Best Buy Q&A and reviewer measurements.
